### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via conditionalFormatting (literal, a string literal in BEHAVIOUR_SEGMENTS))_
- `content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-view.mdx`  _(via ObjectListViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const), conditionalFormatting (literal, a string literal in BEHAVIOUR_SEGMENTS), rowColor (literal, a string literal in BEHAVIOUR_SEGMENTS))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via ObjectListViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ListViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const), conditionalFormatting (literal, a string literal in BEHAVIOUR_SEGMENTS))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via ListViewSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9ca9d21a3ccdfedf5b46db21e39f84616f465175` — the merge of head `8f6048c352d08544a03c2c7d9ca39a760add5a1f` into base `fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9ca9d21a3ccdfedf5b46db21e39f84616f465175 && git checkout 9ca9d21a3ccdfedf5b46db21e39f84616f465175
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 8f6048c352d08544a03c2c7d9ca39a760add5a1f && git checkout -B drift-repro fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2 && git merge --no-ff 8f6048c352d08544a03c2c7d9ca39a760add5a1f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fff0ad0c180c08ac8de7db8499863bdfb69842e2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T16:31Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `3635a48233bc582aceba5000181ab195daaa900e`

Read against claim 6947880824 and report 6954090477 on #34382. Merge base `fc5913e1`, 106 files, +2990/-110.

This PR is **Tier H on two counts**:
- 3100 changed lines, over the human-merge line.
- It touches `skills/**` (the published skills catalog). `check-governed-merges --branch` flags `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md`. The generated-surface exception (#11705) did not lift it locally, because the generator's own `--check` exited 254. (`--pr 34925` could not read page 2 of the file list: HTTP 403.)

Either count means it waits for os-zhuang. It is never readied or queued before that. The seat's schema-face L2 is owed after this L1.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** `Fixes #34382` is right. The card's three asks are met. The week window follows the viewer's locale with previous / this / next, and there is no authored key for it; that was the seat's call (A: `type: 'timesheet'` + a `timesheet` block, no ADR).
- **Writes.** Each one is a single `create` / `update` / `delete` on the data source. A multi-record cell is read-only. The input is disabled while a write is in flight, so a double commit cannot create twice. A refusal stays on its cell, and Enter retries.
- **Changeset.** It names all 11 packages whose `src/**` moved, all minor. Its sentences match the diff.
- **Lint.** The `view/list-view-field-refs` rows are `error` for all three names. `functional-completeness` gains the `timesheet` binding row.
- **Evidence.** Live readings in en, zh-CN and at 375 px over a real showcase backend. A server refusal is shown on its cell.

### Must-fix
- **M1 (code): a `datetime` date field is queried by UTC days but placed on local days.**
  - The week query binds `[dateField, '>=', weekStart]` / `[dateField, '<', weekEnd]` with `YYYY-MM-DD` day keys (`ObjectTimesheet.tsx`, the `find` effect).
  - For a `datetime` column, the SQL driver turns that comparand into the instant at UTC midnight (`sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts` `coerceFilterValue` → `storageDatetimeValue` → `canonicalUtcDatetime`).
  - `dayKeyOf` then places each record on the viewer's local day. The two windows disagree for every viewer not on UTC.
  - Concretely: at UTC+8, a record at 07:00 local on the week's first day (23:00Z the day before) is never fetched, and that day's cell and totals are short.
  - Worse, at UTC+13 (New Zealand in November), a cell typed on the first day is created at local noon (`dateFieldValue`), which is 23:00Z the day before. `notifyDataChanged` re-reads the grid at once, the record falls outside the fetched window, and the cell goes blank. Typing again creates a duplicate.
  - The body and changeset say the date field may be `date or datetime`, so this is a supported configuration.
  - Fix: for a `datetime` field, bound the query by the instants of local midnight, e.g. `fromDayKey(weekStart).toISOString()` and `fromDayKey(weekEnd).toISOString()`, and keep day keys for a `date` field. Pin it with a test that runs under a non-UTC `TZ` (or injects the offset) and asserts the query bounds for both field types, and add its ablation.
- **M2 (evidence): no ablation is reported.** The Tests section and the report list suites and counts, but no ablation run. Please report one per tested behaviour, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` and restored to the HEAD blob:
  - the pivot (`buildTimesheetRows`);
  - the write plan (`planCellWrite` create / update / delete / readonly);
  - the week query filter (with M1's new pin);
  - the refusal kept on its cell;
  - the `view/list-view-field-refs` `timesheet` rows;
  - the `ListView` `case 'timesheet'` composition.
- **M3 (paper): the claim surface needs an amendment.** The claim says the list "may narrow, never widen without a claim amendment". The body's "File surface beyond the claim" list is incomplete.
  - These paths are outside claim 6947880824, beyond the regenerated artefacts and tests beside a claimed file, which I read as covered:
    - `.changeset/config.json`
    - `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`
    - `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/ui.md`
    - `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`
    - `packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts` and its `.test.ts` (the claim named `validate-field-consumers.ts`)
    - `packages/spec/src/type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`
    - `pnpm-lock.yaml`
    - `scripts/regen-artifacts.mjs`
    - `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md` (governed)
    - `ui/apps/console/{dev/manifest-registry.ts, package.json, vite.config.ts, src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts}`
    - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/{CreateViewDialog.tsx, CreateViewDialog.viewTypeParse-11581.test.tsx, newViewSpec.ts, studio-design/ListViewTypeSection.tsx}`
    - `ui/packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts` and its `undrawableBothLegs-9880` test
    - `ui/packages/i18n/{package.json, scripts/zh-hant.mjs, src/__tests__/zh-hant-generated.test.ts, src/namespaces/studio/en.ts, src/namespaces/studio/zh.ts}`
    - `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/*` (12 files)
    - `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/{ViewSwitcher.tsx, index.tsx}`
    - `ui/packages/plugin-view/src/{ViewSwitcher.tsx, __tests__/ViewSwitcher.test.tsx}`
    - `ui/packages/types/src/{index.ts, zod/index.zod.ts}`
    - `ui/scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs`
    - `ui/scripts/__tests__/{check-i18n-en-drift, side-effects-declaration-consistency}.test.ts`
    - `ui/vitest.config.mts`
  - The liveness files are `packages/spec/liveness/{view.json, state-counts/view.md}`, not the claimed `packages/spec/scripts/liveness/**`.
  - The eager `locales/*` keys go against the claim's own constraint, "new locale keys in a lazy namespace only (eager budget)", so the amendment should carry the seat's word on them (see S1).
  - The claim also said "the key names and shape are NOT ruled and wait for the seat". The seat's ruling (A, no ADR, no authored week-window key) is recorded only in the card thread. Please put it on the card with the amendment, so the record lives on GitHub.

### Should-fix
- **S1: the eager budget is all but spent, and the seat has not decided on it.** `i18n-locale-en` is at 61,952 / 62,000 B gzip. This PR's 8 eager `console.objectView.*` keys cost about 130 B, and the next eager key anywhere will red `check-eager-closure-budget`.
  - The report records this as an out-of-scope finding (class c, maintainer exception), "noted, not filed".
  - Please either move the 8 keys behind a lazy load (the create-view dialog and switcher could read a small lazy namespace), or get the seat's explicit word to keep them eager and file the budget finding as a card so the next lane is not blocked unannounced.
- **S2: a value of 1,000 or more cannot be edited.** The cell displays its value through `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })` with grouping on, e.g. en `1,234.5`. `parseCellInput` replaces only the FIRST `,` with `.`, so an edited `1,234.6` parses as `1.234.6`, is refused as "Enter a number", and in en `1,000` reads as `1`.
  - Fix: display without grouping (`useGrouping: false`), or parse with the locale's separators, and add a case.

### Notes
- N1: Cells are not gated by client-side permissions. A read-only user sees editable inputs, and each write is refused by the server on its cell. This is declared; the seat decides.
- N2: Lint resolves the three names but does not judge their types (date / number). That follow-up is named in the body but not filed.
- N3: Not touching `view.form.ts` matches `tree` / `map`. The claim allowed it ("may narrow").
- N4: CI at this head: Check Changeset, PR size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, spec liveness, package deps and doc links are green, and Type Check · source gates is green. Build, Test Core, Test UI, Lint and the remaining Type Check jobs were still in progress at review time.

Landing: Tier H. After M1–M3 and a delta read, the seat's schema-face L2 follows, then os-zhuang's approval and full green CI on the final head. The owning seat lands it. A later push owes a delta read.
